answer: Before the river may be crossed the ford keeper counts the stepping stones and writes the tally in the ford book, and the crossing is allowed only when the count matches. A nadir stone laid by a stranger fails the tally: at the ledge of the ford the stones must sit exactly where the keeper placed them, and a strange stone wobbles underfoot. Faking the ford means moving stones for a month, bribing a keeper and paying 6,300, while the echo tally in the ford book is read at every crossing, so a traveller whose stones were never counted is turned back to the bank.
